Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

main adjective

chief, most important

also chief, principal, the main thing, main point, main road, central (most important), prime (chief), of prime importance, first-rank, leading

classical

Tac. Dial. 28.4: cujus praecipua laus erat tuērī domum
Quint. 1.3.1: ingeniī signum in parvīs praecipuum memoria est

praecipuus, praecipua, praecipuum

adjective

main, chief, principal

The one taken before the others (prae and capiō, Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • caput est — the main thing is

    phrase, with an infinitive or an accusative and infinitive · classical · Cic. Att. 1.17.4: id quod caput est; Cic. de Or. 1.132: caput esse artis decēre (Lewis & Short); Traupman 105: id caput est, that’s the main point

    The main dish of a dinner is caput cēnae (see main dish).

  • 1prīncipālis: long first i (Lewis & Short leaves it unmarked). From prīnceps, which de Vaan derives from prīmus and capiō (p. 489, s.v. prīmus). Traupman 343 marks it.

    prīncipālis1, prīncipāle — principal, chief

    adjective, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Fat. 41: causae … prīncipālēs (Lewis & Short); Traupman 343: via prīncipālis, main road

    In Cicero a term of philosophy, more frequent from Pliny on. Via prīncipālis was the main street of a Roman camp (Liv. 10.33, Lewis & Short).

  • prīmārius, prīmāria, prīmārium — of the first rank, leading, prime

    adjective · also used · classical · Cic. Sen. 61: populī prīmārium fuisse virum; Plaut. Mil. 3.1.73: prīmārius parasītus (Lewis & Short)

    One of the first, chief in rank: a leading man or woman of the city (Cic.); of things, first-rate (Plaut.). Of persons more than of matters; for the main point see caput est above.

Examples

  • cujus praecipua laus erat tuērī domum et īnservīre līberīs

    whose chief praise was to look after the house and devote herself to the childrenTac. Dial. 28.4

  • et, id quod caput est, nōbīs inter nōs nostra sīve incommoda sīve vitia sīve injūriās esse tolerandās

    and, what is the main thing, that we must bear with one another’s annoyances, faults and wrongsCic. Att. 1.17.4

See also major, main dish, important, special.
